_meta.title: Task-Orchestrator Claude-facing surface manifest (read-boundary authority)
_meta.source_of_truth: live task-orchestrator MCP surface; tool read/write/destructive annotations cross-referenced to reports/task-orchestratorrepo-truth-pack/MCP_TOOL_MANIFEST.json (upstream v2.2.0 / 13 tools)
_meta.authority_note: Hand-authored independent contract. scripts/validate_dx_surface.py checks that .claude/commands/dx/*.md conform to THIS file. The manifest is NOT generated from command frontmatter — that is deliberate, so drift in a command is detectable against an independent authority.

classifications.safe_read_only: Idempotent read; never mutates workflow/repo state. The P1 read-surface is exactly these.
classifications.write_non_destructive: Mutates state but does not delete/cascade-terminate existing data.
classifications.write_destructive: Can delete data or cascade-terminate items (destructiveHint=true).

claim_item.note: Present in the live v3 surface; wrapped by no /dx: command. Absent from the upstream v2.2.0 manifest — classification inferred (sets a claim; non-destructive).

reopen.note: Write by intent (reopen a terminal item) but currently wired read-only: the reopen transition was not wrappable at authoring time, so the command only calls get_context today. Classified non-read to keep it out of the read-surface.

implement.note: Composite ADHD session command; calls ConPort/Serena/PAL tools, not the task-orchestrator surface. Uses legacy tool aliases (mcp__zen__*, mcp__serena__*) — an existing inconsistency, out of scope for this catalog packet.

read_command_nonorch_allowlist._note: Non-orchestrator tools a read-class command MAY declare. Fail-closed: any non-orchestrator tool in a read command that is NOT in this list is a violation — this catches a read command gaining a repo-write (Write/Edit) or a bridge/memory write (e.g. mcp__conport__log_decision), which the orchestrator-only check would otherwise miss. 'Bash' is permitted as a general read utility (read commands use it for git plumbing); the validator cannot introspect what Bash does, so this remains a trusted, documented concession (see inventory §4).

boundary.in_scope_read_surface: The 8 read commands above + the 7 safe_read_only tools. These may be used without mutating workflow or repo state.
out_of_scope: no live task-orchestrator writes (manage_*, advance_item, claim_item, create_work_tree, complete_tree)
